---
title: "Estimate costs and compare economic outcomes"
description: "Allocate recorded expenditure and choose completed-interval or full-label outcome accounting."
---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis)
invisible(capture.output(source(system.file(
  "examples", "quickstart.R", package = "TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis"
), local = TRUE)))
```

Recorded cost estimation and future economic assumptions are separate steps.
Examples use the synthetic
[quickstart data](https://github.com/HealthInformaticsUT/TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis/blob/main/inst/examples/quickstart.R):

```{r load-example, eval=FALSE}
source(system.file("examples", "quickstart.R", package = "TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis"))
```

## Estimate expenditure from observed records

```{r estimate-costs}
costs <- estimateStateCosts(histories, cost_records, terminalCostMap = c(Dead = "Stable"))
costs$estimates[c("cost_state", "observed_days", "total_cost", "mean_cost_per_day")]
```

Local records need `subject_id`, `event_date` and `amount`. Estimation does not
need a transition model. Daily means divide recorded amounts by **all observed
state-days**, including days without a cost record. No matching record means
zero recorded cost; a missing amount makes its affected total and mean `NA`.
States without observed days have no estimate. Currencies stay separate.

For your own connected CDM, choose the cost measure and domains explicitly:

```{r extract-costs, eval=FALSE}
cost_events <- extractCosts(
  cdm, histories, measure = "total_charge", domains = c("Visit", "Drug"),
  allocation = "duration"
)
costs <- estimateStateCosts(histories, cost_events)
```

`cdm` is your existing CDMConnector reference. The extractor keeps the connection
open. Visit filters select associated expenditure without changing the observed-day
denominator; qualifying records can select earlier costs from the same visit.
Check whether visit charges already include itemised costs before combining domains.

Start allocation assigns the full charge to `event_date`. Duration allocation
spreads it over the original inclusive service interval; local records also need
`event_end_date`. A seven-day charge of 700 with five resolved observed days
allocates 500 and leaves 200 unallocated. Inspect `allocatedCosts` and
`unallocatedCosts`; sum `amount`, not repeated `original_amount` values.

`terminalCostMap` moves terminal costs **and observed days** to a nonabsorbing
cost state, without changing clinical histories. `adjustCostPrices()` uses a
supplied currency-specific price index before allocation. See the
[price-adjustment example](https://github.com/HealthInformaticsUT/TrajectoryMarkovAnalysis/blob/main/inst/examples/price-adjustment.R).

## Choose the accounting horizon

| Path | Functions | Four weekly steps |
|:--|:--|:--|
| Completed intervals | `createRewardModel()`, `summariseOutcomes()` | Four intervals, 28 days |
| Full cycle labels | `projectCosts()`, `summariseSimulation()` | Five labels, 35 days |

The day totals assume continuous living occupancy. Intermediate stages add no
time. Neither path infers within-cycle death times or a half-cycle correction.

## Account for completed intervals

```{r interval-rewards}
rewards <- createRewardModel(
  stateCosts = c(Stable = 100, Complication = 200, Dead = 0),
  aliveStates = c("Stable", "Complication"),
  utilities = c(Stable = 0.8, Complication = 0.6, Dead = 0),
  currency = "EUR", priceYear = 2026,
  costDiscountRate = 0.035, healthDiscountRate = 0.035
)
reference <- summariseOutcomes(projection, rewards)
outcomeTotals(reference, perPatient = TRUE)
```

State costs are amounts per completed interval. The final endpoint adds no
recurring cost or living time. `costTiming` and `healthTiming` independently
select the start, end or state after a named stage; discount timing is separate.
`transitionCosts` can charge named-stage or net events. `upfrontCosts` applies once.

This path accepts projections and uncosted simulations with explicit starting
states. It rejects fitted entry models and simulations carrying cost rules or
a cost model. The boundary `entryState` used to prepare stage observations is
compatible; it is distinct from a fitted `entry` outcome model.

## Charge full labelled cycles

Raw cost estimates in a bundle are descriptive. Activate fitted healthcare
charging with an explicit cost model:

```{r healthcare-model}
healthcare <- createCostModel(
  costs, unit = "day", currency = "EUR", priceYear = 2026, terminal = "entry"
)
run <- simulateTrajectories(
  createModelBundle(transitions, costs = healthcare), n = 100,
  initial = c(Stable = 1), nSteps = 4, terminalStates = "Dead", seed = 42
)
labelled <- summariseSimulation(
  run, aliveStates = c("Stable", "Complication"),
  utilities = c(Stable = 0.8, Complication = 0.6, Dead = 0)
)
outcomeTotals(labelled, perPatient = TRUE)
```

Daily models integrate a full label, splitting cost periods when needed. Cycle
models multiply the daily mean by the supplied matching cycle length. Terminal
entry charges one full label with `terminal = "entry"`; `"none"` suppresses it.
Initially terminal patients and subsequent terminal residency are not charged.
Manual `costRules` add entry, once, recurring or transition components.

`summariseSimulation()` reads saved charges. Every living label, including the
initial and final labels, contributes full-cycle health time: 52 weekly steps
can represent 53 weeks. Discounting uses recorded label-start `elapsed_day`.
For projections, `projectCosts()` charges stipulated state and net-transition
costs across labels, with no discounting or health calculation. Fitted entry adds
no baseline cycle, although explicit entry fees or transition charges can apply.

## Compare compatible scenarios

```{r compare-outcomes}
intervention_rewards <- updateRewardModel(rewards, upfrontCosts = c(programme = 50))
intervention <- summariseOutcomes(projection, intervention_rewards)
comparison <- compareScenarios(reference, intervention)
comparison$costEffectiveness
```

`updateRewardModel()` replaces entire supplied fields. Comparisons require the
same accounting path and compatible populations, horizons and health definitions.
Use `scenarioCovariates` for explicit treatment-assignment differences. Incremental
values are intervention minus reference. ICERs are reported for positive health
gain and nonnegative incremental cost; dominance receives a separate status.
Uncomputed outcomes stay `NA`. Prices, discount rates and willingness to pay are
analyst inputs. See [interventions and future mortality](interventions-and-future-mortality.html).
